The Federal Communications Commission added foreign-produced humanoid and quadruped robots, along with foreign-produced power inverters, to its "Covered List" of equipment barred from new FCC authorization, according to the [FCC's own fact sheet](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-423682A1.txt). editor_notes.source_verification: All 7 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns). Read every decompressed snapshot in sources/2026-07/fcc-adds-foreign-made-humanoid-robots-and-power-inverters-to-covered-list-targeting-chinas-market-lead/: source-0.html.gz (FCC fact sheet DOC-423682A1) confirms the Carr quote verbatim ('Following President Trump's leadership...') and the 'pose unacceptable risks...' determination language. source-1.html.gz (CBS News) confirms the 85% China market-share figure and the Mao Ning quote verbatim, and confirms the Morgan Stanley $15B-by-2030 forecast and the Pentagon/Unitree military-ties claim. source-2.html.gz (American Bazaar) confirms the 85% figure and the 15,000 total / 5,000+5,000 Unitree-AGIBOT unit breakdown. source-3.html.gz (Route Fifty) confirms the 'remote connectivity capabilities... inherent security vulnerabilities' official quote and the Huawei/ZTE historical Covered List precedent. source-4.html.gz (Gizmodo) confirms the Carr 'lock step' quote and the conditional-approval/no-retroactivity claims. source-5.html.gz (CGTN) confirms the Mao Ning 'protectionism will not enhance US competitiveness' quote in CGTN's own phrasing. source-6.html.gz (Robotics and Automation News) confirms the FCC's own 'mobile robots, such as humanoids and quadrupeds' definition. One misattribution found: the article attributes the quoted phrase 'collect data leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance foreign intelligence capabilities, or to remotely commandeer the robots' to CBS News reporting it 'in similar terms' — this exact language does not appear anywhere in the CBS snapshot (verified: no hits for 'surveil', 'malign', or 'commandeer' in source-1.html.gz). It is in fact a near-verbatim paraphrase of the FCC fact sheet's own language ('Advanced robotic devices collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans...'), which is correctly and separately cited to the FCC elsewhere in the article. This is a real but secondary misattribution (mid-body, not headline/lead) that would ordinarily be correctable rather than disqualifying on its own.
